### Motivation / Background

<!--
Describe why this Pull Request needs to be merged. What bug have you fixed? What feature have you added? Why is it important?
If you are fixing a specific issue, include "Fixes #ISSUE" (replace with the issue number, remove the quotes) and the issue will be linked to this PR.
-->

Fixes #45389.

As documented in the issue linked above, it would be expected that mutations made within `update` callbacks also update the `updated_at` timestamp, especially since this behaviour already occurs with `save` callbacks.

### Detail

This Pull Request ensures that timestamps are **rewritten** once all `update` callbacks have run so that mutations made within them (if any) are recognised as updates, updating the `updated_at` timestamp as a result.

I initially considered just changing the ordering of when timestamps are set to be after all callbacks have been completed, but that would introduce a regression with the changes made [in this commit](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/dddbccb25a709e1897326e2a25d37da83bbfd717) seeing as timestamps always need to be available inside callbacks.

I've also improved coverage for some related tests where timestamps are expected to exist within callbacks. These now test create, update and save callbacks (one type each) and not just a single create callback. I did this because I failed the only test that existed when working on my solution and thought it'd be valuable to cover all 3 of these callback types to ensure no regressions are intorduced.

### Additional information

<!-- Provide additional information such as benchmarks, reference to other repositories or alternative solutions. -->

Shoutout to @markhallen for their debugging efforts and producing a failing test which (which I've stolen for this PR).

issue_context.title: updated_at is not affected by attribute changes in before_update callback
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

* Modify an attribute in a before_update callback.
* call save on an instance of a model with said callback

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile(true) do
  source 'https://rubygems.org'

  git_source(:github) { |repo| 'https://github.com/#{repo}.git' }

  # Activate the gem you are reporting the issue against.
  gem 'activerecord', '~> 6.1.4.1'
  gem 'sqlite3'
end

require 'active_record'
require 'minitest/autorun'
require 'logger'

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: 'sqlite3', database: ':memory:')
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :updaty_posts, force: true do |t|
    t.string :name
    t.timestamps
  end

  create_table :savy_posts, force: true do |t|
    t.string :name
    t.timestamps
  end
end

class UpdatyPost < ActiveRecord::Base
  before_update :mutate_name

  private

  def mutate_name
    return if new_record?

    self.name = 'something different'
  end
end

class SavyPost < ActiveRecord::Base
  before_save :mutate_name

  private

  def mutate_name
    return if new_record?

    self.name = 'something different'
  end
end


class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_association_stuff
    upost = UpdatyPost.create!
    spost = SavyPost.create!

    before_upost_updated_at = upost.updated_at
    before_spost_updated_at = spost.updated_at

    refute_equal 'something different', spost.name
    refute_equal 'something different', upost.name

    sleep 2

    upost.save!
    spost.save!

    assert_equal 'something different', spost.name
    assert_equal 'something different', upost.name

    refute_equal spost.updated_at, before_spost_updated_at, 'changed attribute did not change timestamps in before_save'
    refute_equal upost.updated_at, before_upost_updated_at, 'changed attribute did not change timestamps in before_update'
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior
Based on the warning in [the guide](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_callbacks.html#updating-an-object) 

> Avoid updating or saving attributes in callbacks. For example, don't call update(attribute: "value") within a callback. This can alter the state of the model and may result in unexpected side effects during commit. Instead, you can safely assign values directly (for example, self.attribute = "value") in before_create / before_update or earlier callbacks.

I would expect updated_at to change when changing an attr in a before_update callback.

### Actual behavior
updated_at does not change.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.1.4.1 (but tested my reproduction above in rails 7 with same result)

**Ruby version**: ruby 2.7.6p219 (2022-04-12 revision c9c2245c0a) [x86_64-darwin21]
(but also seen on other ruby 2.7.x versions on heroku-20 stack)

Not sure if this is an actual bug or intended behavior, but I be happy to open a PR against the guides if it's the latter.

**I think** this may be evaluated before the `before_update` callback.

The change is evaluated in `ActiveRecord::Timestamp::_update_record` and a decision is made whether or not to touch the `updated_at` timestamp.

### Using `before_update`

`ActiveRecord::Timestamp::_update_record` is invoked for the `before_update` callback during the `:validate` callbacks and before the change has been made.

During the `:update` callbacks when the new attribute value is committed to the db, `ActiveRecord::AttributeMethods::Dirty::_update_record` is used and the timestamp check is not performed. 

### Using `before_save`

`ActiveRecord::Timestamp::_update_record` is invoked for the `before_save` change during the `:save` callbacks and after the change has been made.

## `before_update` flow

Note that `ActiveRecord::Timestamp::_update_record` is executed before the `name` attribute is updated.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    record.save!-->>validation callbacks: no changes
    validation callbacks-->>validate callbacks: no changes
    validate callbacks->>update callbacks: ActiveRecord::Timestamp::_update_record
    validate callbacks->>update callbacks: record_timestamps = true, partial_updates? = true, has_changes_to_save? = false
    validate callbacks->>update callbacks: should_record_timestamps? = false
    validate callbacks-->>update callbacks: no changes
    update callbacks->>write to db: record.name = "Jack Bauer"
    write to db->>saved: record.name = "Jack Bauer"
```

## `before_save` flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    record.save!-->>validation callbacks: no changes
    validation callbacks-->>validate callbacks: no changes
    validate callbacks-->>save callbacks: no changes
    save callbacks->>write to db: record.name = "Jack Bauer"
    save callbacks->>write to db: ActiveRecord::Timestamp::_update_record
    save callbacks->>write to db: record_timestamps = true, partial_updates? = true, has_changes_to_save? = true
    save callbacks->>write to db: should_record_timestamps? = true
    save callbacks->>write to db: record.updated_at = Time.now
    write to db->>saved: record.name = "Jack Bauer"
    write to db->>saved: record.updated_at = Time.now
```

Here is the failing test that I wrote:

`activerecord/test/cases/timestamp_test.rb`

```ruby
  def test_saving_an_unchanged_record_with_a_mutating_before_update_callback_updates_its_timestamp
    klass = Class.new(ActiveRecord::Base) do
      self.table_name = "developers"

      include Developer::TimestampAliases

      before_update :change_name

      private
        def change_name
          return if new_record?

          self.name = "Jack Bauer"
        end
    end

    @developer = klass.create!
    @previously_updated_at = @developer.updated_at

    travel(1.second) do
      @developer.save!
    end

    assert_not_equal @previous_name, @developer.name
    assert_not_equal @previously_updated_at, @developer.updated_at
  end
```

Only this assertion fails:
`assert_not_equal @previously_updated_at, @developer.updated_at`

review_comments: Regression test for when callbacks are executed without mutations.
Failing assertion:

```suggestion
    assert_not_equal @previously_updated_at, @developer.updated_at
    assert_not_equal @previously_updated_at, @developer.reload.updated_at
```

This ensures that the correct timestamp is persisted, too.
(Should do the same on the other test.)
